(3) DEAD vs FOUND-NOTHING — PRESENT, and it is the script's whole thesis (:25-26 'A DEAD agent and an agent that FOUND NOTHING both come back empty. A fan-out that ignores the difference reports a clean pass over work that never ran.'). Implemented at :96 `const LIVE = new Set(['CLEAN', 'CORRECTED', 'FATAL'])` (an allow-list, so an agent that returns nothing cannot be mistaken for one that found nothing wrong); :194-195 a dead measure ⇒ `status: 'UNMEASURED'` with every lens named UNVERIFIED; :201 a non-live verdict ⇒ `unverified(...)`; :209 `status: named.some(isLive) ? So C4's several 'PARTIAL — death already fail-closed' framings are CORRECT; this one is genuinely closed. (4) NOT_SPAWNED — PARTIAL. It exists, but only for work that never started because the ARGS were wrong: :81-89 `if (problems.length > 0) { log('measure-refute: bad args — spawned nothing: ...'); return { status: 'UNVERIFIED', fatalCount: null, integrity: `0 agents spawned. Nothing was checked. ${problems.join('; ')}`, units: [] } }`, pinned by the two tests at :93-121 asserting `labels.length === 0`. There is NO path that reports work abandoned AFTER the run begins, because no path can abandon it — once pipeline() starts, every remaining unit and lens is spawned regardless of what happened to the previous ones. So a caller can tell 'I never started, here is why' from 'I finished', but never 'I started, then stopped, and here is what I did not do.'
